audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers hand Olaf levels 4-5, first item and 2+ items, giving him 6 of 7 stages in a lane Kayle wins 51.62%. The file's own whys contradict it: whys[3] says the window evens out, whys[5] says Nashor's flips the lane, whys[6] says she out-scales him.
audit.why: Packet levelChart reads Olaf / Olaf / Olaf / Skill / Skill / Kayle / Kayle, matching both the prose and the kit — Olaf is a finite-scaling bruiser and Kayle's first item is where the ranged pattern beats him.
audit.corrected: Row 3 -> Skill, row 5 -> Kayle, row 6 -> Kayle; rows 0-2 and 4 unchanged. Full and content flipped in matched pairs.

audit.why: Four spikes present and correctly sited: Olaf levels 1-3, Kayle 6, Kayle first item (Nashor's), Olaf's Ragnarok all-in as the standing threat.

audit.whatIsWrong: Kayle's W is repeatedly called a shield — 'Celestial Blessing shield', 'W heal-shield', 'his true damage ignores your shield', 'ignore your Q slow and W shield'. Celestial Blessing is a heal plus move speed on a flat 15s cooldown; it grants no shield. Ragnarok is also described as ignoring that shield.
audit.why: Riot's text: Kayle W 'heals and grants Move Speed to herself and the nearest ally'. Reckless Swing deals true damage, which ignores armour and MR — it does not interact with healing at all. Ragnarok grants immunity to disables while he keeps attacking, not heal negation. The distinction matters: a heal can be out-paced by sustained true damage, which is exactly why the pre-6 trade is unwinnable.
audit.corrected: Call Celestial Blessing a heal everywhere; say Reckless Swing's true damage ignores armour and MR; say Ragnarok makes him immune to disables while he keeps attacking.

audit.why: Undertow is a flat 9s that resets on axe pickup, so the 'wait for the cooldown' framing genuinely does not apply to it — the existing advice to dodge the axe rather than count it is right. Ragnarok at 100/90/80s is the countable one and is already the tracked cooldown.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Ragnarok's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Celestial Blessing and Radiant Blast's resist shred even it out, but he still wins the extended trade the moment Undertow lands — neither owns it.

edits.after: Hit Ragnarok to shrug your CC and out-pace Celestial Blessing's heal, diving you under tower before your items land

edits.before: Level 6 is your lifeline — Divine Ascent turns your autos into ranged AoE waves, so for the first time you farm and poke from outside his axe-pickup range and actually kite the all-in he used to win for free. Divine Judgment is your equalizer for his dives: pop it to survive the commit, then W away with the move-speed burst. But be honest about Ragnarok — when Olaf ults he's CC-immune and his true damage ignores your shield, so your invuln only delays him; don't burn R and then stand in his face. Through levels 4-6 it's genuinely even — he still wins a straight melee fight, but you're no longer free to kill.

notes: All three suspectNames are false positives — Reckless Swing, Divine Ascent and Divine Judgment are the correct names. Left alone as unverifiable from the kits: whether Ragnarok's disable immunity also strips Radiant Blast's slow. Riot's text says only 'immune to disables', and slows are conventionally not disables, so the original claim that he 'ignores your Q slow' was removed rather than restated.
